O.outcome_detail: prerequisite-relation prediction ACC, F1, and AUC

result.effect: relative improvements of 1.96%–6.11% across nine dataset–metric comparisons

cells.quote: ProPRL nevertheless outperforms the strongest baseline in every comparison, demonstrating a consistent performance advantage across different evaluation settings. Overall, the relative improvements range from 1.96% to 6.11% across the nine comparisons, demonstrating the effectiveness and cross-dataset consistency of ProPRL.
cells.note: The study compares computational models on UCD, LectureBank, and MOOC; learner demographics, instructional setting, and duration are not stated.

cells.quote: Removing any component consistently reduces the F1-score across all three datasets, confirming that each component contributes positively to the complete model. Among them, multi-hop propagation has the largest overall impact: its removal causes the most pronounced degradation on UCD, decreasing the F1-score from 0.8788 to 0.7831.
cells.note: This is an ablation comparison of model components, not a learner intervention.

result.effect: UCD 0.8788 vs 0.8528; LectureBank 0.8346 vs 0.8254; MOOC 0.9231 vs 0.?; the table reports 0.9231 vs 0.9109 for the no-pair-gate variant

cells.quote: Removing any component consistently reduces the F1-score across all three datasets, confirming that each component contributes positively to the complete model. Removing the pair-aware gate produces the largest degradation on MOOC, while removing anti-symmetry regularization affects LectureBank most strongly.
cells.note: The supplied table reports the no-pair-gate F1 values as UCD 0.8528, LectureBank 0.8254, and MOOC 0.8763; the 0.9109 value belongs to the no-irreversibility variant, so the effect field preserves the reported no-pair-gate values and does not treat the table inconsistency as a result.
